subject: Identity integration matrix and SCIM/RBAC clarifications for Nimbus Bank RFP
messages:
From: Ayesha Rahman <ayesha.rahman@nimbusbank.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: PAM Team <pam-team@nimbusbank.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 15:22:00 -0400
Subject: Request: detailed identity integration matrix and SCIM behavior

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for taking our call earlier. As part of Nimbus Bank's procurement review, the security architecture team needs a concise integration matrix that covers SAML/OIDC SSO behavior, the SCIM provisioning contract (schemas, PATCH support, bulk, rate limits), and RBAC/admin controls (delegated admin, role hierarchies, audit events).

Can you provide a single spreadsheet that maps: supported protocol variants (IdP/SP, SP-initiated, IdP-initiated), endpoint URLs/JWKS rotation cadence, SCIM attribute mapping examples (email, externalId, activated/disabled), TTL/soft-delete semantics, and what audit events are emitted for user/role changes? We also need an example SAML metadata XML and a SCIM flow diagram for our engineers.

Targeting vendor submission by Friday COB (2026-08-14). Appreciate a short cover note that calls out any limitations.

Best,
Ayesha
Senior Information Security Engineer
Nimbus Bank

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Ayesha Rahman <ayesha.rahman@nimbusbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: detailed identity integration matrix and SCIM behavior

Hi Ayesha —

Thanks — we can deliver that. I'm attaching a draft matrix and a SCIM flow SVG; the matrix highlights protocol support and behavioral notes. High-level summary up front:

- SSO: We support SAML 2.0 (IdP/SP, SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows), and OIDC with Authorization Code + PKCE and client credential flows for machine-to-machine. JWKS rotation is supported; we recommend a 24–72 hour automated key rollover with JWK metadata exposed at /v1/.well-known/jwks.json.
- SCIM: Complete User and Group schemas, SCIM PATCH (RFC7644) supported, transactional PATCH for single-user changes, bulk operations limited (recommended page size: 100, bulk size limited via account policy). We provide rate-limit headers and a configurable throttling policy for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- RBAC/Admin: Fine-grained roles in the Console (Admin, IAM Admin, Billing Admin, Read-only Auditor). Support for custom roles (add/remove permissions), role inheritance, and audit events on role/user assignment.

Attachments: nimbus-rfp-identity-matrix.xlsx, redwood-scim-flowchart.svg, sso-metadata-saml.xml

We'll iterate quickly. Marissa — could you validate the matrix rows for SCIM PATCH semantics and include the sample SCIM PATCH request/response examples? Ben — please confirm the exact audit log retention windows for Hosted vs Dedicated customers so we call that out.

Rafael
Director, Security Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:35:00 -0400
Subject: Re: identity matrix — SCIM PATCH and soft-delete semantics

Rafael / Ben,

Reviewed the draft matrix. Notes to include in the submission:

1) SCIM user lifecycle:
- Provision: POST /scim/v2/Users — supports required fields: userName, name.givenName, name.familyName, emails[type=work,value]. ExternalId is optional but recommended for source-of-truth mapping.
- Update: PATCH with operations array is supported; we support 'add', 'replace', 'remove'.
- Soft-delete: We set "active": false in the user's resource and keep the resource for 90 days in Hosted; Dedicated customers can configure retention down to 30 days or up to 365 days. After retention, a hard-delete permanently removes the user.
- Disable vs Delete: We recommend disabling (active:false) for auditability + reversible restores.

2) SCIM group sync:
- Group membership changes emit group.patch events; we support Group.members.add/remove via PATCH.

3) Rate limits / bulk:
- Hosted: 1200 requests/minute per account across SCIM endpoints with 429s on burst; we include Retry-After.
- Dedicated: configurable, typically 10k requests/minute with burst policy. Bulk operations supported via POST /scim/v2/Bulk (max 500 operations per bulk request).

4) SCIM security:
- OAuth2 bearer tokens for SCIM endpoints (client credentials). Support for mutual TLS for Private deployments.

I'll add short request/response examples to the matrix. Ben — can you confirm audit retention text?

Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Identity Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: identity matrix — audit retention and RBAC exports

Marissa — quick confirm:

- Hosted: Audit logs (user/role changes, SCIM events, SSO logins) retained for 180 days by default; exported logs available via Console (CSV/JSON) and via an API endpoint /audit/v1/events.
- Dedicated: 3 years retention option (enterprise contract) with S3-compatible export.
- Private: customer-managed retention per KMS/HSM policy; we support forwarding to SIEM via syslog/HTTPS with configurable event schemas.

RBAC: Console supports role templates, and we expose an RBAC export (roles.json) with role->permission mappings. We will include a sample roles.json in the Drive link.

Ben
Principal Product Engineer — Security
Redwood Inference

From: Ayesha Rahman <ayesha.rahman@nimbusbank.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: PAM Team <pam-team@nimbusbank.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Identity integration matrix and SCIM/RBAC clarifications for Nimbus Bank RFP

Rafael —

Received the spreadsheet and the flowchart — thank you. A couple of follow-ups from our architecture review:

1) SAML metadata: Can you confirm whether metadata endpoints support metadata signing and how Redwood handles IdP certificate rollover (are there overlapping validity windows)?
2) SCIM: For soft-delete, confirm whether the user's externalId is preserved on re-provision (i.e., if user re-provisions after hard-delete, will externalId be reused or a new resource ID be created?).
3) RBAC: We need to know whether Redwood supports SCIM Group-to-Role automated mapping (i.e., if a group is created/updated in the IdP and provisioned to Redwood, can we map that group to a role automatically or does it require a manual mapping in the Console?).

If possible, a one-paragraph answer addressing these three points would be great so we can include it in the RFP appendix.

Best,
Ayesha
Senior Information Security Engineer
Nimbus Bank
